navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire ABC cluster — Curaçao↔Bonaire (~30 nm), Curaçao↔Aruba (~50 nm), and the day cays — with the bonus of year-round, below-the-hurricane-belt operation.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) is optional here — useful only for longer reaches toward the Venezuelan islands or onward Caribbean links; the core ABC network is all Pioneer II.

precedents.why_it_matters: Year-round operation materially improves Pioneer II unit economics relative to hurricane-belt nodes.

regulatory_note: All within the Dutch Kingdom (Aruba and Curaçao are constituent countries; Bonaire is a Dutch public entity), with Maritime Authority Curaçao and the respective port authorities. Bonaire National Marine Park strongly favors zero-emission, low-wake vessels.
seasonality: A standout: below the main hurricane belt, the ABC islands operate year-round, with steady trade winds. This is the most weather-robust cluster in the region for Pioneer II.

summary: Aruba, Curaçao and Bonaire lie off the Venezuelan coast, below the main Atlantic hurricane belt — which makes the ABC islands a rare Caribbean cluster with year-round calm-season economics. The three islands sit ~30–50 nm apart (Pioneer II range), with strong cruise and resort volume on Aruba and Curaçao and world-class dive tourism on Bonaire. Today inter-island travel means a flight; there is no fast passenger ferry, making the ABC link a clean greenfield corridor.
tagline: The Dutch Caribbean trio that sits below the hurricane belt — a rare year-round island-hopping cluster.
